Who we are

Equal opportunity for every child, youth and family.

We work to improve the lives of underprivileged and poverty-stricken children, youth and adults in the communities we serve.

  • We believe everyone deserves equal opportunities and a high quality of life, with long-term, transformative and sustainable outcomes.
  • We transform lives and uplift communities through comprehensive training programmes and developmental support.
  • Our mission is to give people the knowledge, skills and resources they need to thrive in their personal and professional lives.
  • Our focus on community development aims for a positive, sustainable impact that reaches far beyond individual success.
Our purpose EmpowerEngageInspireImpactTransform

What guides us

Our values

  • Integrity

    Championing empowerment and sustenance.

  • Community first

    Uplift and strengthen communities.

  • Education & empowerment

    Equip youth with the skills and the knowledge to thrive.

Vision

A community that reaches its full potential.

We envision a community where individuals are empowered to reach their full potential and where social and economic inequalities are overcome. We create lasting, positive change by upskilling the community to sustain their livelihoods.

Mission

Empower communities. Transform lives.

Our mission is to empower communities and transform lives by providing comprehensive support, resources and opportunities to individuals facing adversity. Through our programmes, initiatives and partnerships, we aim to break down barriers, foster self-sufficiency and promote social inclusion.

With a commitment to equality, compassion and sustainable practices, we work tirelessly to create lasting change, address systemic issues and build a brighter future for all.

Golf

2026 Players’ Assistant Training Program

The 2026 Players’ Assistant Training Program is a flagship fundraising and employment programme designed to move unemployed youth and persons with disabilities (PWD) into sustainable career pathways within the country-club ecosystem. A joint initiative by the Vice Projects (Pty) Ltd, this structure bridges the gap between untapped local talent and operational roles across golf courses, clubhouse hospitality, retail and club administration. By offering comprehensive golf readiness, customer service and role-specific training, the programme delivers measurable social impact, community safety enhancements, and shared economic growth for participating clubs.

Rugby

Mac Masina Foundation

The Mac Masina Foundation is a Soweto-based non-profit organisation that uses sports as a tool for social change, youth development, and community upliftment. Founded on the belief that athletics can serve as a lifeline against poverty, violence, and unemployment, the foundation specifically targets youth aged 14 to 35.

In partnership with

FableReads

Stories children love. Full of wisdom and lessons for life.

Karabo-le-Musa works in partnership with FableReads, a collection of hundreds of fables from around the world. Children can read or listen in multiple languages, and find a story by the value or theme it explores.

Read & listenFor freeNo advertising

Screen time done differently

Read or listen offline and create your own playlists. Designed to help children pause and think, building literacy and empathy as they go.

Buy a book, gift a book

A collection of timeless favourites with questions and activities. Buying a book also helps bring more stories to more children.

Partner with us

From community initiatives to global sponsors, FableReads is looking for partners in financing, implementation and development to expand access to stories for children everywhere.

Want to know how FableReads and Karabo-le-Musa can work with your school, group or organisation? Write to us and we will connect you.

Our community

How we work

Built with the community, step by step.

  1. Fundraising and donor engagementA strategy to secure financial support for our initiatives and programmes.
  2. Partnerships and collaborationWorking with other non-profits, businesses, government agencies and community organisations to reach a broader audience.
  3. Volunteers and communityBuilding a strong volunteer base and strong relationships with the community.
  4. A sustainable foundationFor continuous learning, adaptation and dedication.

How we listen

  • Needs assessmentCollecting data on the most pressing issues, such as health disparities, education gaps and unemployment.
  • Demographic analysisLooking at age, gender, income, education and cultural background to fit programmes to the people we serve.
  • Community forumsMeeting residents to share our work and hear their input.
  • Pilot programmesTesting a programme with community members before a full launch.
  • Impact assessmentTracking outcome indicators and evaluating programmes after they run.
  • Trend analysisFollowing local, regional and national trends that affect the community.

Every programme has clear objectives, timelines and performance indicators. We allocate budget, staff and volunteers to run each one well, review outcomes regularly and adjust so the work stays true to our mission.
